stories.headline: Colorado Speaker-elect Bacon picks Brown, Garcia for Joint Budget Committee
stories.summary:
House Speaker-elect Jennifer Bacon of Denver has chosen Reps. Kyle Brown of Louisville and Lorena Garcia of Adams County as the House Democratic caucus's representatives on the Joint Budget Committee. The six-member panel crafts the state's annual spending plan and includes two members from each chamber's majority party and one from each minority.

House Minority Leader Jarvis Caldwell announced that Rep. Rick Taggart of Grand Junction will continue as the House Republican representative. Senate Republicans have yet to name their pick; Sen. Barbara Kirkmeyer of Brighton has served four years on the committee. Sen.-elect Emily Sirota of Denver was appointed by Senate Democrats, and Sen. Judy Amabile of Boulder is likely to chair in 2027. The changes follow the departure of Sen. Jeff Bridges, who was elected state treasurer.

Bacon said Garcia was chosen in part for her work on Amendment 87, the graduated income tax measure voters approved last week. Garcia is CEO of the Colorado Statewide Parent Coalition, a major backer of the measure. Bacon also cited Brown's healthcare expertise, as the committee is expected to look for about $1.6 billion in general funds to cover an anticipated 2027-28 deficit, driven largely by Medicaid spending.

stories.headline: Business worries grow in Colorado after graduated income tax passes
stories.summary:
After Amendment 87 passed by a relatively slim margin, business leaders and analysts are voicing concern about its effect on growth at a time when Colorado appears to be struggling to attract investment. The measure replaces the state's flat 4.4% income tax with six brackets ranging from 3.7% for lower earners to 8.4% for incomes above $1 million.

New revenue, expected to exceed $2 billion once the measure takes full effect over a tax year, is designated for public education, healthcare and early childcare. Supporters note that most filers would receive a tax break. Opponents say the campaign focused on individual taxpayers and glossed over long-term effects on businesses.

Boulder entrepreneur Dan Caruso, a Level 3 Communications founder who led a spring campaign on the state's competitiveness, said jobs would go to states such as Texas, Arizona and Utah. Carl Koelbel of Koelbel and Company predicted lower demand for office space and housing, citing Denver's net out-of-state migration in 2025. Real estate agent Deviree Vallejo warned of downstream effects on the housing industry.

stories.headline: Colorado businesses outline fixes after state dinged for business climate
stories.summary:
Frustration over Colorado's business climate has built for years, culminating in a data-heavy report last month from the Governor's Competitiveness Council, a public-private partnership led by business leaders and advocates. The report includes about 50 recommendations drawn partly from summer listening sessions.

Lauren Roberts, CEO of Colorado Sun Tofu, which moved its manufacturing to Trinidad about three years ago, said the state's plumbing and electrical permitting led to inspectors ordering work redone years after earlier sign-offs. She also co-owns Denver restaurants Watercourse Foods and City O' City.

Many recommendations need funding, such as designating site-ready locations, or legislative changes, such as simplifying sales and use taxes, redesigning incentives and letting multi-agency permit reviews run concurrently. There is no simple measure of how many companies have left over the climate, and Colorado is still landing new ones, though other states are seen as more aggressive. Roberts and others said they want to stay and hope for cheaper, easier operations.

stories.headline: Denver pedestrian dies after being struck near 9th Street and Auraria Parkway; driver cited
stories.summary:
A man was killed Wednesday morning when a vehicle struck him on 9th Street near Auraria Parkway in Denver. The crash occurred around 11:35 a.m., according to Denver Police Department spokesman Pablo Sanchez.

The pedestrian, who has not been identified, was taken to a hospital, where he later died. The 24-year-old driver was cited for careless driving resulting in death, a misdemeanor.

The fatality remains under investigation, police said.

stories.headline: Multiple people hospitalized after crash near 6th Avenue and I-25
stories.summary:
The Denver Police Department reported Wednesday evening that a crash near eastbound 6th Avenue and Interstate 25 resulted in at least one serious injury. Multiple people were taken to a hospital.

Police did not immediately release details on the cause of the crash or the condition of those hurt. The investigation was continuing.

stories.headline: Jamal Murray scores 30 as Nuggets hold off Grizzlies 123-118
stories.summary:
Jamal Murray scored 17 of his 30 points in the fourth quarter as the Denver Nuggets held off the Memphis Grizzlies 123-118 on Wednesday. Nikola Jokic added 27 points, 11 rebounds and eight assists, and Denver improved to 6-4 after a ten-point loss to Houston.

The Nuggets led by as many as 18 points before Memphis cut the margin to two with under a minute left. Cam Johnson scored 23 points on 9-of-15 shooting and made timely plays down the stretch.

Denver committed only six turnovers to Memphis's 12 and held a 15-2 edge in points off turnovers. Nine Nuggets recorded a block, with Murray and Aaron Gordon each rejecting two shots. The Grizzlies have lost four of five after a six-game winning start.

stories.headline: Landeskog scores twice as Avalanche beat Maple Leafs 6-3
stories.summary:
Gabriel Landeskog scored twice, including the tiebreaking goal at 5:02 of the third period, as the Colorado Avalanche beat the Toronto Maple Leafs 6-3 on Tuesday at Scotiabank Arena. Landeskog's winner came 51 seconds after Toronto tied the game at 3-3, redirecting a Nazem Kadri pass.

Devon Toews had a goal and an assist, Cale Makar added two assists, and Mackenzie Blackwood made 28 saves. Artturi Lehkonen scored at 17:15 and Martin Necas added an empty-netter.

Colorado improved to 11-6-2 and has points in six of its last seven games. Toronto, at 8-10-2, has lost four in a row. Coach Jared Bednar called it close to a 60-minute effort.

stories.headline: Avalanche's new Landeskog-Kadri-Roy line emerging as a weapon
stories.summary:
Coach Jared Bednar recently said publicly he was unhappy with the Avalanche's play and would make changes. One result is a new line of Gabriel Landeskog, Nazem Kadri and Nicolas Roy, which was prominent in Tuesday's 6-3 win over Toronto.

The trio helped produce two of Colorado's key goals. Landeskog scored late in the first period after a Roy rebound opportunity, and later scored the go-ahead goal on a Kadri pass 51 seconds after Toronto tied the game.

Bednar said the group's strength should be below the tops of the circles in the offensive zone while staying responsible. Colorado is 11-6-2 and has won five of its last seven, and the line adds depth behind the top group of Nathan MacKinnon, Martin Necas and Artturi Lehkonen.

stories.headline: Warm, dry Veterans Day in Colorado; weekend rain and snow chances ahead
stories.summary:
Colorado is in an unseasonably warm stretch, with temperatures 10 to 15 degrees above normal through the end of the week. Highs are expected near 70 degrees on Thursday and Friday as a ridge of high pressure moves east across the state, with clouds increasing Friday.

A storm system is expected to reach southwestern Colorado and northern New Mexico Saturday evening, bringing snow to the mountains above 8,000 feet and scattered showers to the plains. Highs on Saturday and Sunday should dip to the mid- to upper 50s.

Monday looks pleasant before another system arrives midweek. Long-range models show a stronger system late next week that could bring Denver its first flakes of the season.

stories.headline: Denver dining: Casa Bonita plaza sold, new fall menus and dessert fundraiser for puppies
stories.summary:
The Lamar Station Plaza in Lakewood, a 271,632-square-foot strip mall and parking lot surrounding Casa Bonita, has been sold, according to the Denver Business Journal. The new owners plan to update the facade and signage, replace the roof and improve the parking lot. Matt Stone and Trey Parker still own Casa Bonita.

Jovanina's Broken Italian is donating 50% of dessert sales through the end of the year to Rocky Mountain Puppy Rescue. Pig and Tiger in Five Points has introduced holiday-inspired Taiwanese dishes, including General Tso's Squash and Apple Pie Shaved Ice.

The Salty is running a limited menu with Tache pistachio milk from Nov. 13 to 22, and JING in the Denver Tech Center has rolled out a new menu.

topStory.headline: Zelenskyy Says Starshield Speed Limits Have Returned as US Envoys Meet Putin in Moscow
topStory.summary:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Thursday that the Ukrainian military is again experiencing significant disruptions to Starshield, the military version of SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet service. In a post on X, he said units have reported the problem for several days along the entire front line and in Russian-occupied areas. He described "systematic speed restrictions" that limit the service to 161 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour), and said Ukrainian military investigators concluded the limits were not random errors. NBC News reported that the system normally runs at a stable speed above roughly 250 mph. SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Zelenskyy said the restrictions complicate the interception of Russian jet-powered drones, and that some strikes have gotten through because Ukrainian interception systems cannot reach sufficient speeds to respond in time. "Unfortunately, this is helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes against Ukraine," he said, adding that Kyiv is trying to establish the circumstances with the American side. Ukraine first raised alarms about speed limits on Starshield last month. At that time, Elon Musk placed responsibility on President Donald Trump, who has been pressing Kyiv to make concessions to end the war. The U.S. government said only Musk could have made such a decision, and Trump denied involvement. Around the same period, Ukraine accused the U.S. of failing to share intelligence on incoming Russian attacks, which the White House denied.

The renewed complaint came as U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin. Kirill Dmitriev, Putin's special envoy, greeted them at their plane and accompanied them to central Moscow, where talks began a few hours later. The visit followed two days of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, which ended Wednesday with no breakthrough but with an agreement on a large prisoner exchange. They were the first direct Russia-Ukraine negotiations mediated by the U.S. in nine months. The U.S. said differences remain on major issues, including territory, though some progress was made on post-war security guarantees.

Kushner said after the Abu Dhabi session that "there's no trust right now between the sides." He said the purpose of the Moscow meeting was to finalize plans for more humanitarian relief and prisoner releases, and to push to add Europeans to the format to make it multilateral. Al Jazeera's reporter in Moscow said the delegation was bringing an updated peace proposal, and that Moscow has insisted on talks without European participation. Kyiv has strongly rejected Putin's demand that Ukraine surrender all of the eastern Donbas region in return for peace. Reporting from Kyiv indicated Ukrainians expect little from the Moscow talks, noting that the main significance of the Abu Dhabi round was that it took place at all.

Elsewhere, leaders from more than 40 European countries gathered in Dublin on Thursday for a European Political Community summit focused on continental security. Zelenskyy, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte attended, and participants were expected to discuss the Abu Dhabi talks. French European Affairs Minister Delegate Benjamin Haddad said the EU will approve additional sanctions against Russia. Kushner and Witkoff are scheduled to meet Zelenskyy in Dublin on Friday after their Moscow talks, while fighting continues on the front lines, where neither side has made significant gains in months.
